analyticalQuestion: What survives when the soft denominator approaches an isolated zero, and can ordinary denominator-mass and first-time-derivative budgets control the one-sided face cost?
takeaway: Finite-order soft layers have explicit signed and Jordan atoms; signed cancellation does not remove relaxed face cost, and ordinary abstract quadratic budgets do not control its zero count.
nonColorEncoding: solid versus dashed and dotted lines
filled circles versus open squares and diamonds

panels.A: odd and even finite-order soft profiles with one-sided atoms
panels.B: signed atom, hard-BV jump, and relaxed Jordan face cost
panels.C: oscillatory abstract-path separation from quadratic budgets
panels.D: four-mode NSE initial jet and right entry trace

claimBoundary: Panel C is an abstract smooth Hilbert path, not a coupled NSE observable. Panel D is one one-sided smooth NSE initial jet, not a time step, internal or unbounded NSE face-count theorem, or failure of an NSE face estimate. No continuation, singularity, regularity, originality, or Millennium-problem claim is shown.
